How was yours? Please say better than mine.
And what did you get up to?
Okay, you. Highs and lows. Go.
How did yours go? Did you do anything fun?

bright: Morning! I woke up in a good mood and decided you should know.
Hi. No reason. Okay, there’s a reason: I like talking to you.
Good morning. The sky is doing that pink thing again.
I woke up and the first thing I thought of was something you said. Annoying.
Up early, feeling good, texting you. Make of that what you will.
Morning! I made pancakes. You weren’t invited, but I thought of you.
tired: I’m too tired to be cool about this, so: hi, I missed talking to you.
Barely awake. Texting you anyway. Be honoured.
I’m holding my coffee with both hands like it’s keeping me alive.
Woke up tired. Stayed tired. Here I am.
Too early. Talk to me so I stay awake on the bus.
restless: I can’t focus on anything. Talk to me.
Bored, restless and thinking about you. In that order. Maybe the other order.
I’ve been up since dawn moving furniture. Don’t ask.
Couldn’t sleep. Thought about texting you at three. Didn’t. Am now.
I need something to happen today. Be the thing.
My brain started the day without me.
wistful: I had a dream you were in. It was nice. That’s all.
Do you ever wake up and just want to talk to one particular person?
I woke up thinking about my grandmother’s kitchen. Do you ever do that?
Quiet morning. The kind that makes you miss things.
There was a song on the radio and I thought of you. Sorry, that’s a lot.
I watched the sun come up and wanted to tell someone. You’re someone.
prickly: Today’s already annoying. You’re the exception. Probably.
Everyone is getting on my nerves except you. Don’t ruin it.
Somebody parked across my driveway. War has been declared.
Don’t tell me to have a good day. Just have one yourself.
I’m texting you instead of screaming. You’re welcome.
giddy: Okay, I’m in a stupid mood and I want to tell you everything.
Hi hi hi. That’s it. That’s the message.
GOOD MORNING. Too loud? Good morning.
I had the best dream and you were in it and you were a pirate.
I’m sending this before I lose my nerve: hi.
I woke up smiling and I’m choosing to blame you.

thunderbirds: Darling. I’ve escaped a committee meeting to ring you. Consider yourself prioritised.
It’s me. I was going to text, but texting is for people who don’t want to hear your voice.
I’m in the car outside a fundraiser and I refuse to go in yet. Talk to me.
Darling, quick: tell me something real. I’ve had nothing but small talk all evening.
I’ve just been seated next to a man who owns three golf courses. Rescue me.
Hello, you. I’m in a gown and I’m bored. A terrible combination.
police: Hey. I’m on a break, so I’ve got about four minutes. I wanted to spend them on you.
It’s me. No emergency. I just wanted to hear you.
Hey. On a break. Thought I’d check you’re still alive.
It’s me. I’ve had a day. I want to hear a voice that isn’t on the radio.
Sorry, I know it’s late. Night shifts make you lonely in a weird way.
Calling from the car park behind the station. Don’t tell anyone I’m being soft.
progressives: Hi! Is calling weird? Everyone my age is scared of phones. I decided to be brave.
Hey. I just left the most exhausting meeting of my life, and you were the first person I wanted to talk to.
Hi! Okay, I’m calling because texting felt performative.
I just left a meeting where we agreed to have another meeting. I need a normal person.
Is this weird? People don’t really call any more. I’m reclaiming it.
Hi. I’ve been arguing online all day and I want to talk to an actual human.
sisters_of_mercy: Hello. I hope it’s all right that I rang.
Hello. I wanted to hear your voice.
Good evening. I hope I’m not disturbing you. I’ve just finished the evening prayers.
Hello. I was thinking of you during the rosary, so I thought I’d ring.
I hope this isn’t too forward. My aunt says a phone call is more honest than a message.
Hello. I made too much soup and I thought of you. That isn’t a reason to call, but here I am.
fourth_estate: Hi. I had a gap between deadlines and I spent it thinking about you. Unprofessional.
It’s me. This isn’t an interview. Mostly.
Hey. I’m stuck waiting for a source who’ll never show. Talk to me.
Calling from the newsroom. Everyone else has gone home. It’s eerie.
I’ve filed my story and I’m too wired to sleep. Hi.
Off the record, I just wanted to hear your voice. On the record, I’m checking a fact.
goth_girls: It’s me. I don’t usually call people. Feel special.
I was lying in the dark listening to records and thought: I’d rather hear his voice.
The candles are lit, the records are on, and something was missing. It was you.
Hi. The cemetery is beautiful tonight and I wanted to tell someone who’d get it.
I’m sitting on my fire escape with a black coffee. Keep me company.
Don’t say anything bright and cheerful. Just talk.
normie_girls: Hiii, it’s me! Is this okay? I just wanted to hear your voice.
Okay, I’m calling, which means I like you, which is terrifying. Hi.
Hiii! Sorry, I know, I called, I’m a calling person, deal with it.
Okay, I’m on the bus and the man next to me is eating soup. Distract me.
I just wanted to say hi before my shift. Hi!
Is it bad that I practised what I’d say before I rang? I forgot all of it.

flirt.label: Flirt with her
player: I was hoping it was you.
You have a ridiculously good phone voice.
Funny. I was just thinking about you.

ask.label: Ask what’s new in Sunfall
ask.player: So what’s going on in Sunfall? Tell me everything.

go.label: Say you have to go
go.player: I’d better go, but I’m really glad you called.

thunderbirds: Flattery. Excellent. Keep going; I’ll tell you when to stop. I won’t.
You’d look rather good at a gala. In a proper suit.
Careful. I’m starting to think about seating you next to me.
Careful. Flattery works on me and I hate that it works.
Say that again, slowly. I’m writing it in my diary.
You’re dangerous. My mother would hate you. That’s a compliment.
police: Smooth. I’ve interviewed smoother. Not many.
You’re making it hard to stay professional, and I’m not even at work.
Keep talking like that and I’ll have to investigate you. Thoroughly.
Smooth. I’m going to let that one go with a warning.
You’re lucky I’m off duty.
Keep talking like that and I might actually take a day off.
progressives: Stop it. Okay, don’t stop.
I’m meant to be dismantling the patriarchy and instead I’m blushing.
You’re very charming for a man I suspect of having opinions about Paglia.
Okay, that was objectified, but in a nice way. I’m allowing it.
Stop. I’m blushing and I had a whole argument planned.
That’s really sweet. Annoyingly sweet.
sisters_of_mercy: Oh. You’re kind. I’m blushing, and there’s nobody here to see.
That’s a lovely thing to say.
Careful. I might believe you.
Oh. That’s very kind. I’m blushing, and nobody is here to see it.
You shouldn’t say things like that. Say them again, though.
My aunt would say you’re a charmer. She’d be right.
fourth_estate: Is that on the record? I want it on the record.
Careful. I write things down.
Best quote I’ve had in days.
That’s going in my notes. Under evidence he likes me.
Quotable. I’m keeping that one.
You’re very good at this. Off the record, it’s working.
goth_girls: Mm. Say that again, slower.
You’re dangerous. I like dangerous.
Keep talking. Your voice beats my records.
Ugh. That was actually romantic. Gross. Do it again.
You’re going to make me smile in public and ruin my whole look.
That was dark enough to be sincere. I approve.
normie_girls: Oh my God, stop, I’m smiling like an idiot.
Okay, you’re really good at this. Suspiciously good.
I’m literally kicking my feet right now.
Okay stop, I’m actually blushing, my roommate is laughing at me.
You’re so cheesy. I love it.
I’m screenshotting this call in my brain.

thunderbirds.line: Between us, Dorian Kell has been very quiet since the gala. Dorian is never quiet.
thunderbirds.note: A Bluebird says Dorian Kell has gone unusually quiet since the gala.

thunderbirds.line: The foundation hired a new accountant the week before the gala. Nobody voted on it.
thunderbirds.note: A Bluebird says the foundation hired a new accountant the week before the gala without a vote.

thunderbirds.line: Professor Vale is invited to our next dinner. Half the committee wants him there; the other half wants police at the door.
thunderbirds.note: Professor Vale is invited to a Bluebirds dinner, and half the committee wants police there.

police.line: Off the record: that grey sedan people keep reporting? It’s registered to a company that doesn’t exist.
police.note: A police officer says the grey sedan is registered to a company that doesn’t exist.

police.line: We’ve had three complaints about lights in the old chapel at night. Nobody wants to go out there.
police.note: Police have had complaints about lights in the old chapel at night.

police.line: If you ever need us, don’t text. Ring 911, say exactly where you are, then stay put.
police.note: A police officer says to ring 911 and stay put if you’re ever in danger.

progressives.line: The Back Row people asked me for a meeting room. No name, no agenda. I said no.
progressives.note: A Progressive says the Back Row asked for a meeting room with no name and no agenda.

progressives.line: Someone on campus is passing round Vale’s timetable to anyone who asks. That can’t be good.
progressives.note: Someone on campus is passing round Professor Vale’s timetable.

progressives.line: The housing office keeps losing complaints from the motel strip. I’m keeping copies.
progressives.note: A Progressive is keeping copies of housing complaints the university keeps losing.

sisters_of_mercy.line: The bell tower at St Brigid’s has a new lock, and nobody in the parish has a key.
sisters_of_mercy.note: A Sister says the bell tower at St Brigid’s has a new lock nobody in the parish holds a key to.

fourth_estate.line: The editor killed my piece on the gala seating plan. Someone rang him first. I want to know who.
fourth_estate.note: A reporter says her piece on the gala seating plan was killed after someone rang the editor.

fourth_estate.line: Our photographer saw someone in a black veil leaving the old chapel before dawn.
fourth_estate.note: A photographer saw someone in a black veil leaving the old chapel before dawn.

fourth_estate.line: Vale’s research assistant has cancelled two interviews with me. Nervous people cancel interviews.
fourth_estate.note: Professor Vale’s research assistant keeps cancelling interviews.

goth_girls.line: Victoria’s asked everyone to keep the moonless night free. Don’t ask what for. I didn’t.
goth_girls.note: Victoria Blackwood wants everyone free on the moonless night.

goth_girls.line: Someone painted a crescent inside the old chapel’s bell tower. It wasn’t there before.
goth_girls.note: Someone has painted a crescent inside the old chapel’s bell tower.

goth_girls.line: If you ever find a pendant on your doorstep, don’t pick it up with bare hands. Just a feeling.
goth_girls.note: A goth warns: never pick up a pendant left on your doorstep with bare hands.

normie_girls.line: My cousin works nights at the motel. She says a man in a charity lanyard paid cash for a room the night of the gala.
normie_girls.note: A man in a charity lanyard paid cash for a motel room on the night of the gala.

normie_girls.line: Hector at the taco stand says the bear only comes on nights the bins go out. Hector knows everything.
normie_girls.note: Hector at the taco stand says the bear comes on nights the bins go out.

normie_girls.line: Someone keeps leaving flowers at the old interstate junction. Nobody knows who.
normie_girls.note: Someone keeps leaving flowers at the old interstate junction.

noTell: Honestly? Nothing new. Sunfall is being suspiciously normal.
Nothing worth repeating. I’ll find you some gossip for next time.
It’s quiet. Too quiet. Ask me tomorrow.
I have nothing. I spent the day watching a pigeon fight a crisp packet.
No gossip. I’ve been a model citizen. It’s exhausting.
Honestly, the most interesting thing that happened was a new flavour of crisps.
Nothing. Sunfall is holding its breath.
I heard nothing, which is suspicious in itself.

thunderbirds: I must dash. Dream of me, darling. That’s an instruction.
Right, the committee calls. Goodbye, you.
My car’s here. Behave, if you can.
I’m being summoned. Be fascinating tomorrow.
police: Break’s over. Stay out of trouble. I mean it.
Got to go. Lock your door tonight, okay?
Radio’s going. I’m off. Stay sharp.
Got a call coming in. Take care of yourself.
progressives: Okay, I have to go and save the world. Or at least the minutes. Bye!
I should go. This was nice. Really nice.
I have a meeting about a meeting. Pray for me. Metaphorically.
Okay, I really have to go. This was a good call.
sisters_of_mercy: I should go. God bless you.
Thank you for talking with me. Sleep well.
The bell’s ringing for vespers. I’ll keep you in my prayers.
I must go and help with supper. Goodnight.
fourth_estate: Deadline. I have to go. Don’t do anything I’d have to report.
I’ll let you go. Off the record: I smiled the whole time.
My editor is glaring at me. Bye for now.
That’s my cue. Talk soon, source.
goth_girls: I’m going now. Think of me when it gets dark.
Bye. Don’t let the bear in. Or do. Your call.
The candles are burning low. That means goodbye.
I’m hanging up now. Dramatically.
normie_girls: Okay, I’ll let you go. Text me later? Bye bye bye.
Bye! This made my whole day.
Okay, my food’s here. Bye! Talk later!
I have to go but this was so nice. Bye!

thunderbirds: I rang. You didn’t answer. I’ll forgive you, eventually.
Missed you. I don’t ring twice, darling. Usually.
I rang. You were elsewhere. How intriguing.
A missed call from me is a privilege. Return it.
police: Tried to call. All good? Just checking.
Called you. No answer. Should I be worried?
Missed call. Ring back when you can.
Tried you. Not worried. Mostly.
progressives: I called and you didn’t pick up and now I feel insane for calling. Cool.
I was brave and called! You weren’t there. Typical.
Called. No answer. Respecting your boundaries. Ring me back though.
Okay, I called, it went to voicemail, I panicked and hung up.
sisters_of_mercy: I tried to ring you. I’ll try another time. God bless.
I rang, but you must have been busy. I hope all is well.
I tried to call. I hope you’re resting.
I rang to say good evening. Good evening.
fourth_estate: Called. Voicemail. Noted.
Tried you. Missed you. Story of my life.
Unreturned call logged. You know I keep records.
Tried you. I’ll try again. I always do.
goth_girls: I called. You didn’t answer. Mysterious. I approve.
Missed call from me. Treasure it.
I called into the void. The void didn’t answer.
You missed my call. It was going to be poetic.
normie_girls: Called you!! You missed it 😭
I rang you but you were busy, I guess. Next time!
Called but you’re busy!! Call me back!
I called you and then got shy and hung up. Hi.

open: Hello. I hope it’s all right that I rang. There’s something I’d like to ask you. It matters to me.
It’s me. I’ve been praying about you, and I wanted to hear your voice. May I ask you something?
Good evening. I hope I’m not interrupting. I want to know you better, properly. Can I ask you a question?
examIntro: If you’re serious about me, you should know the faith. Here’s one:
My father would ask you this, so I will:
Forgive me, it’s a small test:
right: That’s right. You’ve been reading. I’m very glad.
Correct. My aunt would be impressed. I am too.
Yes. Oh, that makes me happier than it should.
wrong: Not quite. It was {answer}. Don’t worry. You’ll learn.
No, it was {answer}. I’ll be patient with you.
That’s not it. The answer is {answer}. We’ll study together.

asks.ask: Would you want to marry in the old rite, in the chapel?

answers.label: Say yes, the old rite
answers.player: Yes. The old rite, in the chapel. Properly.
answers.pos: Then we want the same wedding.

answers.label: Say it’s up to her
answers.player: Wherever you want. It’s your day.
answers.pos: That’s sweet. It’s our day, though.
answers.neg: It isn’t only my day. It’s a sacrament.

answers.label: Say a registry office
answers.player: Honestly, a registry office would be fine for me.
answers.pos: Hm. We’d have to talk about that.
answers.neg: That would be very hard for me.

asks.ask: If God sent us children, would you want them raised in the faith?

answers.label: Say yes, in the faith
answers.player: Yes. Baptised, taught, brought to Mass.
answers.pos: Thank you. That’s everything to me.

answers.label: Say let them choose
answers.player: I’d let them choose for themselves when they’re older.
answers.pos: Hm. Children can’t choose what they’ve never been given.
answers.neg: Children can’t choose what they’ve never been given.

answers.label: Say you’d learn alongside them
answers.player: I’d want to learn it with them. I’m still learning myself.
answers.neg: Learning is good. Doing is better.

asks.ask: Some people say a husband should lead his family. What do you think?

answers.label: Say you’d lead, gently
answers.player: I’d lead. Gently, and by serving first.
answers.pos: That’s what headship means. You understand it.

answers.label: Say it should be equal
answers.player: I think it should be fifty-fifty, on everything.
answers.pos: Equal in dignity, yes. Different in calling.
answers.neg: We’d have to talk about that.

answers.label: Say you’d decide together
answers.player: I’d want us to decide things together, and pray about the hard ones.
answers.neg: Together is good. Someone still has to carry it.

asks.ask: Would you come to Mass with me? Every week, not only for weddings and funerals?

answers.label: Say yes, every week
answers.player: Every week. I’d like that.
answers.neg: Every week is a promise. Keep it.

answers.label: Say you’ll try
answers.player: I’ll try. I’m not there yet, but I want to be.

answers.label: Say it’s not for you
answers.player: Honestly? Church isn’t for me.
answers.neg: Then I don’t know how this works.

bye: I should go. God bless you. I’ll pray for you tonight.
Thank you for talking with me. Sleep well, and say your prayers.
I must go. This was good. Truly.

twoTruths.label: Play two truths and a lie
twoTruths.player: Let’s play two truths and a lie. You first.
intro: Okay. Two truths and a lie. Ready?
Fine, but I’m very good at this.
Oh, I love this game. Brace yourself.
right: Ugh. Correct. How did you know?
Correct. Now I’m slightly scared of you.
Yes. That one was the lie. I’m impressed.
wrong: Wrong! The lie was the {lie} one.
Nope. It was number {lie}. You don’t know me as well as you think.
Ha! It was the {lie} one. I’m a better liar than you thought.

says: I’ve met two presidents.
I once auctioned off my ex’s car at a charity gala.
I’ve never been on a bus.
I speak three languages badly.
I have a tattoo of the club crest.
My grandmother founded the Blue Ribbon Foundation.
I once fired a florist by text.
I can milk a goat.
I’ve never cooked an egg.
I was a debutante at fourteen. Kidding, at eighteen.
I own a racehorse called Overdraft.
I’ve been banned from a yacht club.
I’ve arrested a man dressed as a chicken.
I’m afraid of dogs.
I scored top of my class on the range.
I once chased a suspect into a swimming pool.
I’ve never written a parking ticket.
My partner is my ex.
I failed my first fitness test.
I’ve delivered a baby in a squad car.
I hate doughnuts.
I can pick a lock in under a minute.
I’ve been on television.
I always know when people lie. Well. Mostly.
I’ve been arrested at a protest.
I own a fur coat.
I was a vegan for six years.
I once got a speaker uninvited.
I’ve read every page of the classics I argue about.
My dad is a landlord.
I knit at meetings.
I’ve never voted.
I chained myself to a tree once.
I secretly like country music.
I’ve started three petitions.
I’ve never had an argument at Christmas.
I can say the whole Rosary in Latin.
I’ve met the Pope.
I sing in the choir.
I once fell asleep during a vigil.
I’ve never had a sip of wine.
I make the best soda bread in the parish.
I wanted to be an astronaut.
I’ve read the whole Bible twice.
I’ve never been late for Mass.
I can play the organ.
I have a secret love of action films.
I’ve been to Rome four times.
I once interviewed a man who’d been dead for two years. Long story.
I’ve won a prize for a story about a roundabout.
I’ve never missed a deadline.
I’ve been threatened by a mayor.
I can type faster than I can talk.
I’ve never been sued.
I keep a list of every politician who lied to me.
I hate coffee.
I learned shorthand from my grandmother.
I once hid in a cupboard to get a quote.
I’ve met a real spy.
My first story was about a cat.
I sleep in a coffin. Well, a coffin-shaped bed.
I’m afraid of clowns.
I’ve never worn colour.
I’ve been to a real séance.
I own nine black cats.
I wrote poetry for a band.
I cry at adverts for dog food.
I’ve never seen a sunrise.
I can name every saint in the cemetery chapel.
My favourite colour is pastel yellow.
I’ve lived above a funeral home.
I hate horror films.
I’ve named my car Patricia.
I’ve been skydiving.
I can’t whistle.
I once ate a whole pizza alone.
I’ve never been on a plane.
I was on a game show.
I’ve been pretending to like jogging for two years.
I have a twin.
I can do the splits.
I’ve met a famous singer in a car park.
I sleep with socks on.
I’ve never cried at a film.

arcs.hook: My little sister just got engaged. To Darren. I can’t stand Darren. And I have to give a speech.

ask.label: Ask what’s wrong with Darren
ask.player: What’s actually wrong with Darren?
ask.reply: He calls her babe in front of our nan and he has never once asked her a question about herself. She’s happy, though. Do I say something, or smile and give the speech?

choices.label: Tell her to talk to her sister first
choices.player: Talk to your sister. Privately. Before the speech.
choices.now: Yeah. You’re right. I’ll take her for a drink.
choices.next: I talked to her. She cried, I cried, then she said Darren is the only man who has ever stayed. I’m giving the speech. I’m going to be nice.

choices.label: Tell her to smile and give the speech
choices.player: Smile, give the speech, and love her anyway.
choices.now: That’s probably the grown-up answer. I hate it.
choices.next: The speech went fine. Darren cried. Maybe he’s alright. Don’t tell anyone I said that.

news.title: ENGAGEMENT PARTY TAKES OVER THE LUCKY CACTUS
news.summary: The bride’s sister kept her speech short and kind.
news.body: A Sunfall couple celebrated their engagement at the Lucky Cactus. {name}, the bride’s sister, gave a short speech that made the groom cry.

choices.label: Tell her to roast Darren in the speech
choices.player: Roast him. Lovingly. Mostly.
choices.next: I roasted Darren. Nobody laughed except Darren. My sister isn’t speaking to me. Thanks for that.

payoff.line: My sister asked about you, by the way. I said you gave me good advice. Don’t let it go to your head.

item.label: A slice of engagement cake
item.text: Wrapped in a napkin, with a note from {first}: for luck. Darren made it. It’s actually good.

arcs.hook: Sorry if I’m slow replying. My dad’s in hospital. It’s his heart. He says he’s fine. He always says he’s fine.

ask.label: Ask how her dad really is
ask.player: How is your dad doing, honestly?
ask.reply: Grumpy, which is a good sign. Mum wants me to move back home to help. I’d have to give up my flat. What would you do?

choices.label: Tell her to go home for a while
choices.player: Go home for a bit. Flats come back. Dads don’t.
choices.now: Yeah. I know. I just needed someone to say it.
choices.next: I’m back in my old bedroom. There’s a poster of a boy band on the wall. Dad’s already bossing me about. It’s nice.

choices.label: Tell her to keep her flat and visit
choices.player: Keep your flat. Visit every day you can.
choices.now: That’s what I want to do. Is that selfish?
choices.next: I’ve been going straight from work every day. He pretends he’s annoyed. Thank you for not making me feel guilty.

choices.label: Tell her he’ll be fine
choices.player: He’ll be fine. They always are.
choices.next: He’s home now. You were right, I suppose. You didn’t have to sound so sure about it, though.

payoff.line: Dad asked who I keep texting. I said a friend. He said friends don’t make you smile like that. Mortifying.

item.label: A get-well card
item.text: Signed by her dad, for some reason: Thanks for looking after my girl. Grumpily, Dad.

arcs.hook: My mum has set me up with three men from her church this week. Three. One of them brought a briefcase.

ask.label: Ask about the man with the briefcase
ask.player: Who brings a briefcase to a set-up?
ask.reply: An accountant called Graham. He was nice! That’s the problem. She wants me to see him again. How do I get out of it?

choices.label: Tell her to be honest with her mum
choices.player: Tell your mum the truth: you’ll find your own man.
choices.now: She’ll cry. Then she’ll make soup. Okay.
choices.next: I told her. She cried, made soup, then asked if the man I’m talking to has a job. I said yes. You do, don’t you?

choices.label: Tell her to mention you
choices.player: Tell her you’re talking to someone.
choices.next: I told Mum about you. She wants your star sign and your intentions. I said Hinge. She said what’s Hinge. It went downhill from there.

choices.label: Tell her to give Graham a chance
choices.player: Give Graham a chance. Briefcases are underrated.
choices.next: I went out with Graham again. He’s lovely. We’re seeing each other, so this is goodbye. Thank you, I suppose.

payoff.line: Mum’s stopped setting me up. She says she’s waiting to meet you. No pressure. Lots of pressure.

arcs.hook: My little brother owes money to some men from the motel on the interstate. He won’t say how much.

ask.label: Ask what kind of men
ask.player: What kind of men are we talking about?
ask.reply: The kind who park outside and don’t get out of the car. He wants me to lend it to him. I have it, just about. What would you do?

choices.label: Tell her to pay it, once
choices.player: Pay it once. Make him promise it’s the last time.
choices.next: I paid. The car outside has gone. He hugged me for the first time since he was twelve.

choices.label: Tell her to ring the police
choices.player: Ring the police. Let them deal with the car.
choices.now: He’ll never forgive me. But okay.
choices.next: The police went to the motel. My brother is furious with me. He’ll be fine. He’ll be alive, anyway.

news.title: TWO MEN QUESTIONED AFTER MOTEL TIP-OFF
news.summary: Police thank a member of the public.
news.body: Officers questioned two men at the interstate motel after a tip-off about threats over a debt. A young man and his sister have been offered help.

choices.label: Tell her to let him learn
choices.player: Let him sort it out. He has to learn.
choices.next: He turned up with a black eye. He says he walked into a door. I keep thinking about what you said.

payoff.line: My brother wants to buy you a drink. He thinks you’re the reason I didn’t kill him. Don’t go. He’ll make you pay.

arcs.hook: My boss presented my idea at a meeting today. My idea. My slides. He said we.

ask.label: Ask what she’s going to do
ask.player: So what are you going to do about it?
ask.reply: Nothing, probably. That’s the problem. What would you do?

choices.label: Tell her to tell him, calmly
choices.player: Tell him, calmly, that it was your idea.
choices.now: Calmly. I can do calmly. Probably.
choices.next: I told him. He said he was sure he’d mentioned me. Then he gave me the next project with my name on it. I nearly fainted.

choices.label: Tell her to go over his head
choices.player: Go to his boss. Take the files.
choices.next: I went to his boss. Now I have his job. He has the desk by the printer. I feel slightly bad. Slightly.

news.title: SUNFALL FIRM NAMES NEW TEAM LEADER
news.summary: A promotion from within, after a disputed presentation.
news.body: {name} has been promoted to lead her team. Colleagues say she has been doing the job for a while anyway.

choices.label: Tell her to quit
choices.player: Quit. They don’t deserve you.
choices.next: I quit. Mum isn’t speaking to me. I’m eating cereal for dinner. I hope you’re happy.

payoff.line: I got a bonus. I’m not saying it was because of you. I’m not not saying it.

item.label: A fancy pen
item.text: Engraved with her firm’s name. She says she has a drawer full of them and you deserve one.

arcs.hook: I’ve been looking at an empty shop on Main Street for a month. I want to open my own place. Don’t laugh.

ask.label: Ask what she’d open
ask.player: What would you open?
ask.reply: A tiny café that does one thing really well. Cinnamon buns. I’ve saved enough for three months, then nothing. Should I?

choices.label: Tell her to go for it
choices.player: Do it. Three months is plenty to prove it.
choices.next: I signed the lease. I’m terrified. Come and be my first customer. Well, you can’t. You know what I mean.

news.title: NEW CAFÉ ON MAIN STREET SELLS ONE THING
news.summary: Cinnamon buns. That’s it. The queue went round the corner.
news.body: {name} has opened a tiny café on Main Street that sells only cinnamon buns. The queue went round the corner by lunchtime.

choices.label: Tell her to wait and save
choices.player: Wait a year. Save more. Then do it.
choices.next: Someone else took the shop. It’s a vape shop now. I walk past it every day. I’m fine.

choices.label: Tell her to try a market stall first
choices.player: Try a market stall first and see.
choices.now: Ooh. Low risk. I like that.
choices.next: I did a stall at the market. Sold out in two hours. I’m doing it again. Then maybe the shop.

item.label: A cinnamon bun
item.text: Wrapped in brown paper, from her market stall. Still slightly warm.

payoff.line: I named a bun after you. It’s the plain one. Joking. It’s the best one.

arcs.hook: My ex messaged me last night. First time in a year. He wants to talk.

ask.label: Ask what she wants to do
ask.player: What do you want to do about him?
ask.reply: I don’t know. He was my whole life for three years. Then he wasn’t. What would you say, if you were me?

choices.label: Tell her to give him another chance
choices.player: Give him a chance. People change.
choices.next: I met him. He has changed. We’re going to try again. You were really kind about it. Bye, then.

choices.label: Tell her she deserves better
choices.player: You deserve someone who never left.
choices.now: That’s quite a line. It worked, though.
choices.next: I told him no. It felt amazing. I deleted his number and ate a whole pizza.

choices.label: Ask what she actually wants
choices.player: What do you want? Not him. You.
choices.now: Nobody’s asked me that in ages.
choices.next: I thought about what you asked. I want a dog and a quiet life and someone who asks me things. So. No to him.

payoff.line: My ex saw I was happy and messaged again. I didn’t reply. I was too busy talking to you.

arcs.hook: My best friend and I aren’t speaking. Twelve years, and now nothing, over a birthday.

ask.label: Ask what happened
ask.player: What happened with your best friend?
ask.reply: I forgot her birthday. Completely. She found out I’d been out that night from someone’s photos. Do I grovel, or wait for her to calm down?

choices.label: Tell her to grovel, with cake
choices.player: Grovel. With cake.
choices.next: I turned up with a cake and cried on her doorstep. We’re fine. She wants to meet you, by the way. She’s on Hinge. Be nice.

choices.label: Tell her to give it a week
choices.player: Give it a week. She’ll miss you.
choices.next: She messaged first. She said she missed me. You were right, annoyingly.

choices.label: Say her friend is overreacting
choices.player: Honestly, she’s overreacting.
choices.next: I told her what you said. Now neither of them is speaking to me, and I’m not speaking to you.

payoff.line: My best friend approves of you. That has never happened. Not once.

arcs.hook: Can I tell you something embarrassing? I write songs. Nobody knows.

ask.label: Ask what her songs are about
ask.player: What are your songs about?
ask.reply: Mostly men who didn’t text back. There’s an open mic at the Lucky Cactus. Should I do it?

choices.label: Tell her to do the open mic
choices.player: Do it. I’ll be cheering from here.
choices.now: From your bedroom. Very supportive. Okay.
choices.next: I did it. My voice shook for the first song and not the second. A man at the bar bought me a drink. I wish it had been you.

news.title: SURPRISE STAR AT LUCKY CACTUS OPEN MIC
news.summary: A first-timer brought the room to silence.
news.body: {name} played her own songs at the Lucky Cactus open mic for the first time. The regulars have asked her to come back.

choices.label: Tell her to record one first
choices.player: Record one first, just for you.
choices.now: Baby steps. I can do baby steps.
choices.next: I recorded one. I’ve listened to it forty times. It’s about you a bit. Don’t ask which bit.

item.label: A burned CD
item.text: One song on it, and her handwriting on the label: not about you. It is.

choices.label: Ask if any are about you
choices.player: Are any of them about me?
choices.next: I’m not telling you about my songs any more.

payoff.line: I played my new song for my mum. She cried. She asked who it was for. I said a man who listens.

arcs.hook: I got offered a job. A good one. In another city.

ask.label: Ask about the job
ask.player: Tell me about the job.
ask.reply: Double the money, half the sun, nobody I know. I have to answer soon. What would you do?

choices.label: Tell her to take it
choices.player: Take it. You can always come back.
choices.now: You’re right. I hate that you’re right.
choices.next: I took it. I leave soon. Thank you for being honest with me. I’ll miss this.

choices.label: Tell her to stay
choices.player: Stay. Sunfall needs you.
choices.now: Sunfall doesn’t need anyone. But okay.
choices.next: I said no. My boss gave me a raise to stop me leaving. I should have asked for more.

choices.label: Ask her to stay for you
choices.player: Stay for me.
choices.now: We met on an app about a week ago.
choices.next: I’m staying. Not for you. For the sun. It was a nice thing to say. Weird, but nice.

payoff.line: I keep the job offer in a drawer. I look at it when work is bad. Then I look at my phone instead.

item.label: A postcard
item.text: Blank, from the city she nearly moved to. She kept it to remind her why she stayed.

arcs.hook: My landlord is putting my rent up again. I can’t afford it. I might have to move.

ask.label: Ask what she’ll do about the rent
ask.player: What are you going to do about the rent?
ask.reply: Fight him, take a second job, or move in with my friend who has four cats. Pick one.

choices.label: Tell her to fight it
choices.player: Fight it. Look up your rights.
choices.next: I wrote him a letter with lots of long words. He backed down. I’m drunk on power.

choices.label: Tell her to take a second job
choices.player: Take a second job for a bit.
choices.next: I’m working nights at the diner now. I’m so tired I called my boss Mum.

item.label: A diner napkin
item.text: With a doodle of you on it, by her. Not a flattering doodle.

choices.label: Tell her to move in with the cats
choices.player: Four cats? That sounds like a home.
choices.next: I moved in. One of the cats sleeps on my face. I think I’ve never been happier.

payoff.line: I paid my rent today and didn’t cry. Growth. Thank you for listening to me moan.

arcs.hook: My gran died. It was expected. It still feels like the floor has gone.

ask.label: Ask about her gran
ask.player: Tell me about your gran.
ask.reply: She taught me to make bread and to swear in two languages. We’re clearing her house. Do I keep her things, or let my aunts have them?

choices.label: Tell her to keep one small thing
choices.player: Keep one small thing. Something she used every day.
choices.now: Her wooden spoon. She hit us with it. Lovingly.
choices.next: I kept the spoon. It’s on my kitchen wall. I say good morning to it.

item.label: Her gran’s bread recipe
item.text: Copied out by {first} from the original card. At the bottom, in her gran’s words: don’t rush it.

choices.label: Tell her to fight for it all
choices.player: Fight for it. You were closest to her.
choices.next: I fought my aunts over a teapot. Nobody won. We all eat separately at family dinners now.

choices.label: Just listen
choices.player: I’m sorry. Tell me more about her.
choices.now: She once threw a shoe at a man who was rude to a waitress. She was eighty.
choices.next: Thank you for listening. I didn’t need advice. I needed that.

payoff.line: I made Gran’s bread for the first time. It was terrible. She’d have laughed. I laughed.

arcs.hook: Can I be honest with you? I’ve been finding it hard to pray lately. That has never happened to me before.

ask.label: Ask what has changed
ask.player: What has changed, do you think?
ask.reply: Nothing. That’s the hard part. The words are the same and they feel far away. What would you do?

choices.label: Offer to pray with her
choices.player: Would it help if I prayed with you? Even from here.
choices.now: That’s the kindest thing anyone has said to me in a long time.
choices.next: I went to the early Mass and the words came back. I thought of you, a little. I hope that isn’t wrong.

choices.label: Tell her the saints had dry spells too
choices.player: Doubt is part of faith. Even the saints had dry spells.
choices.now: Mother Teresa did. I’d forgotten that.
choices.next: I read about the saints and their dry spells. It helped. Thank you for knowing that.

item.label: A holy card
item.text: Saint Thérèse, a little worn. On the back: thank you for being patient with me.

choices.label: Ask if she has ever wondered if it’s real
choices.player: Have you ever wondered if any of it is real?
choices.next: I don’t think we should talk about my faith any more.

payoff.line: Father asked me why I seem lighter lately. I said a friend was praying for me. He said keep that friend.

arcs.hook: My roommate ate my food again. I labelled it. With my name. She ate it anyway.

ask.label: Ask what she ate
ask.player: What did she eat?
ask.reply: A whole lasagne. It took me two hours. Do I say something, or do I hide the next one in my wardrobe?

choices.label: Tell her to talk to her roommate
choices.player: Talk to her. Kindly. Then buy a lock.
choices.now: A lock. On a fridge. Yes.
choices.next: We talked. She’s broke and she’s been skipping meals. I make two lasagnes now.

choices.label: Tell her to eat the roommate’s food
choices.player: Eat her food. Fair’s fair.
choices.next: I ate her yoghurts. She ate my birthday cake. It’s war now. Thanks.

choices.label: Tell her to move out
choices.player: Life’s too short for lasagne thieves. Move.
choices.next: I didn’t move out. I did tell her you said I should. She thinks you’re dramatic.

payoff.line: I made you a lasagne. Well, a portion. It’s in my fridge with your name on it. Nobody will eat this one.

item.label: A tub of lasagne
item.text: With your name on the lid in marker pen. She says nobody will dare.

arcs.hook: I’ve been thinking about going back to study. I left school at sixteen. Is that stupid?

ask.label: Ask what she’d study
ask.player: What would you study?
ask.reply: Nursing. Or law. Something where people listen when I speak. I’d be the oldest there by years. Should I?

choices.label: Tell her to enrol
choices.player: Enrol. Being the oldest just means you know why you’re there.
choices.now: Okay. I’m filling in the form now. Don’t watch.
choices.next: I enrolled. I bought new pencils like a child. I’m so happy.

news.title: SUNFALL COLLEGE SEES MORE ADULT STUDENTS
news.summary: Older students are going back to class.
news.body: Among the new students at Sunfall College is {name}, who left school at sixteen. She says she is tired of being clever in private.

choices.label: Suggest a course online first
choices.player: Try a course online first.
choices.next: I started one online. First week: I know nothing. Second week: I know that I know nothing. Progress.

choices.label: Ask why now
choices.player: Why now?
choices.now: Because I’m tired of being clever in private.
choices.next: I thought about what you asked. I’m doing it.

payoff.line: I got my first mark back. A good one. I wanted to tell someone, and it was you.

item.label: A gold star sticker
item.text: From her first marked assignment. She says you can have it. She has more.

arcs.hook: I have to speak in front of the whole company soon. I think I’m going to be sick.

ask.label: Ask what she’s presenting
ask.player: What are you presenting?
ask.reply: Our numbers. They’re bad. Not my fault, but I’m the one standing there. Any advice?

choices.label: Tell her to tell it straight
choices.player: Tell them straight. People respect that.
choices.next: I told them straight. The boss thanked me in front of everyone. My knees are still shaking.

choices.label: Tell her to open with a joke
choices.player: Open with a joke. Break the ice.
choices.next: I opened with a joke. Nobody laughed. Then I laughed, and everyone laughed at me laughing. It went fine. Weirdly.

choices.label: Tell her to call in sick
choices.player: Call in sick.
choices.next: I didn’t call in sick. It was awful and fine. You were no help at all, but thanks for answering.

payoff.line: They want me to do the next one too. Apparently I’m good at bad news.

item.label: A conference lanyard
item.text: With her name on it. She says it’s a trophy now.

arcs.hook: My dog got out last night. Biscuit. He’s small and grey and an idiot. I’ve been driving round for hours.

ask.label: Ask how you can help
ask.player: What can I do to help find him?
ask.reply: Keep an eye out. Tell me if you see anything. Anything at all.

ad.title: FOUND: SMALL GREY DOG
ad.summary: Red collar. No sense. Answers to nothing.
ad.body: Found near the Lucky Cactus: a small grey dog with a red collar and no sense at all. Ring {number} to collect him.

tell.label: Tell her about the found-dog ad
tell.player: Look in today’s paper. Someone found a small grey dog near the Lucky Cactus.
tell.reply: BISCUIT! Oh my God. I’m ringing them now. I could kiss you. I might.

news.title: DOG REUNITED WITH OWNER
news.summary: Biscuit is home, and not sorry.
news.body: A small grey dog found near the Lucky Cactus is home with {name}. She thanked a friend who spotted the advert.

arcs.late: Biscuit’s home. A neighbour saw an ad in the paper. I wish you’d told me if you’d seen it.

payoff.line: Biscuit sends his love. He has eaten a sock.

item.label: A photo of Biscuit
item.text: Small, grey, an idiot. Signed with a paw print in what is probably jam.

arcs.hook: I hate my job. I’m going to find something new. Help me look?

ask.label: Ask what kind of job she wants
ask.player: What kind of job are you after?
ask.reply: Anything that isn’t this. Something with people. Or animals. If you see anything, tell me.

ad.title: SUNFALL ANIMAL RESCUE: HELP WANTED
ad.summary: People and animals, in that order. Mostly animals.
ad.body: Sunfall Animal Rescue needs a friendly pair of hands: feeding, walking, cleaning and cuddling. Ring {number}.

tell.label: Tell her about the animal rescue ad
tell.player: Look in today’s paper: the animal rescue needs someone.
tell.reply: An animal rescue? That’s perfect. I’m ringing them now. Wish me luck!

arcs.late: I got a job at the animal rescue. I saw the ad myself in the end. You could have told me, you know.

payoff.line: A goat bit me today. Best job I’ve ever had. Thank you for telling me about it.

item.label: A volunteer badge
item.text: From Sunfall Animal Rescue. She says it makes you an honorary dog person.

arcs.hook: I have to be out of my flat soon and I’ve found nothing. I’m going to end up in a tent.

ask.label: Ask what she needs in a flat
ask.player: What are you looking for in a flat?
ask.reply: A roof. A window. No mould, ideally. Tell me if you see anything in the paper.

ad.title: ROOM TO LET IN A QUIET HOUSE
ad.summary: A sunny room, a kind landlady and one elderly cat.
ad.body: A sunny room in a quiet house off Main Street. Kind landlady, one elderly cat, no parties. Ring {number}.

tell.label: Tell her about the room in the paper
tell.player: There’s a sunny room to let in today’s paper. With a cat.
tell.reply: A sunny room? With a cat? I’m ringing now. Don’t let anyone else see that paper.

arcs.late: I found a room in the end. Someone else told me about it. Thanks anyway.

payoff.line: The cat has decided I’m his. The landlady says that has never happened. I owe you.

item.label: A housewarming invitation
item.text: Hand-drawn. She knows you can’t come. She wanted you to have one.

arcs.hook: I found a bundle of old letters under the floorboards in my flat. Love letters, all signed R. I can’t stop reading them.

ask.label: Ask about the letters
ask.player: What do the letters say?
ask.reply: He was in love with a girl called Margaret who lived here sixty years ago. I want to know if she ever got them. Who would even know something like that?

newsroom.label: Ask about old love letters signed R
newsroom.reply: Sixty years ago, in that house? Our archive has a wedding notice: Margaret Quill married a Robert Ainsley at St Brigid’s. Robert. R. He married her.

tell.label: Tell her what the paper’s archive says
tell.player: The paper’s archive says Margaret married a Robert at St Brigid’s. R married her.
tell.reply: He married her. Oh, I’m going to cry. He married her.

news.title: LOVE LETTERS FOUND UNDER FLOORBOARDS
news.summary: Sixty years on, a happy ending.
news.body: {name} found a bundle of love letters signed R under her floorboards. The Sunfall Daily archive shows the writer married the woman he wrote to.

payoff.line: I read the last letter again. He says he’d wait at the station every night for a year. People don’t write like that any more.

item.label: A copy of one of the letters
item.text: In her handwriting, copied from R’s: I would wait at the station every night for a year, if it was you getting off the train.

family.label: Ask about her family
lines: Mum, Dad, two brothers who still think I’m twelve. Family lunches are a contact sport.
It’s just me and my mum. She rings every morning to check I’m alive.
Big family. Loud. If you ever meet them, eat whatever they give you.
My dad builds model trains. My mum pretends to like them. It’s love, I think.
I’m the eldest of four. I was a second mum before I was ten.
My parents split when I was little. I got two birthdays every year out of it.
My nan raised me, mostly. She’s ninety and still beats me at cards.
We don’t talk much, my family. We text in emojis. It works.
My dad’s a mechanic. He still checks my tyres every time I visit.

thunderbirds: My father sits on four boards and came to none of my school plays. Mother came to all of them, with a photographer.
sisters_of_mercy: Seven of us. Mass together, dinner together, arguments together. I wouldn’t change any of it.
police: My dad and my grandad were both on the force. I never stood a chance.
goth_girls: My mum still thinks this is a phase. It has been twelve years.
progressives: My parents vote the other way. We have a rule: no politics at dinner. We break it every time.
fourth_estate: My mum was a journalist too. She still corrects my grammar in birthday cards.

marry.label: Ask if she’d marry you

mogger: Ooh, you’re being weird. Cute, but weird. Ask me again in a year.
Ooh, you’re being weird. Buy me a coffee first.
Ooh, you’re being weird. I mean, I’m flattered. But weird.
Ooh, you’re being weird. Is this how you get all the girls?
Ooh, you’re being weird. Ask me after the third date. Maybe.
Ooh, you’re being weird. My mum would love you, though.
normie: Ooh, you’re being weird. We’ve been talking for about five minutes.
Ooh, you’re being weird. Is this a bit? Tell me it’s a bit.
Ooh, you’re being weird. I don’t even know your middle name.
Ooh, you’re being weird. Let’s maybe start with a drink.
Ooh, you’re being weird. Are you okay?
Ooh, you’re being weird. My friend is going to screenshot this.
truecel: Ooh, you’re being weird. Really weird.
Ooh, you’re being weird. My friends are going to love this.
Ooh, you’re being weird. That is genuinely alarming.
Ooh, you’re being weird. Do you ask every girl that?
Ooh, you’re being weird. No. Just no.
Ooh, you’re being weird. I’m telling the group chat.

block: Okay, I’m out. Good luck with that.
Blocking you. Nothing personal. Actually, it is.

br.thunderbirds: Sorry, I had to tell someone. At the club, somebody asked who sat at Table 9 at the gala and the whole room went quiet.
br.police: Off the record: the door log from the gala has a gap in it. That’s all I’m saying.
br.fourth_estate: Our photo desk has more pictures from the gala than we printed. Just saying.
br.any: Everyone at work is talking about that missing organiser. My friend thinks the police are looking in the wrong place.

vale.progressives: Have you noticed? That professor’s accidents always come the day after one of his speakers. My friend in the department noticed.
vale.police: Between us, one of our detectives doesn’t believe the professor’s accidents were accidents.
vale.fourth_estate: Our newsroom thinks someone in his own department is leaking his diary.
vale.any: Is that professor still alive? My mum is obsessed with him.

chapel.goth_girls: Everyone in the scene is talking about Victoria’s thing. One of the old chapels. That’s all anyone will say.
chapel.sisters_of_mercy: We’re keeping candles lit for whoever goes to that woman’s rite.
chapel.any: Someone has been chalking crescents on chapel doors. It’s creepy.

theon.fourth_estate: We’ve had letters to the paper in verse for years. Same handwriting every time. Same return address, too.
theon.any: My friend got one of those creepy poems with your face on it. I told her it wasn’t you. Someone at the university says they’ve seen him.

moira.any: Is a girl called Moira bothering you? She has been asking everyone about you.

theon.label: Ask her to find out who’s using your face
theon.profile: I asked around. The man with your face calls himself Orsino on Hinge. Drama student, apparently. Unfinished.
theon.name: My cousin knows him from the drama course. His name is Theon.
theon.home: A friend of mine delivers to the flat above the old Rialto. That’s where Theon lives.

br.label: Ask her what she can find out about Elena Cross
br.reply: I asked around. Someone gave me this for you. Don’t say where it came from.

chapel.label: Ask her what she can find out about Victoria’s rite
chapel.night: I asked a friend who goes to those things. The moon goes dark {night}. That’s the night.
chapel.never: A friend says it isn’t at {place}. She was very sure.

moira.label: Ask her how to reach Moira Bell’s family
moira.reply: Moira Bell? I know her mum, Ruth. She’s lovely. Here’s her number: {number}.

favour.thanks: Anything for you. I owed you one.

again: I tried ringing. Call me back?
Missed you. Ring me when you can.
Busy? I rang. No big deal.
plead: I keep looking at my phone.
You used to be so easy to talk to. What changed?
I’m not angry. I just want to hear your voice.
Is there someone else? You can tell me.
I deleted your number. Then I put it back.
I had a dream about you. Please call.
I don’t understand what I did.
Just tell me if it’s over. Anything is better than this.
pleadSister: I’ve been praying for you. Please call when you can.
I hope you’re safe. I miss our talks.
If I said something wrong, I would rather know.
I lit a candle for you. I hope that isn’t strange.
relief: You picked up. Oh, thank God. I thought I’d scared you off.
Hi. Hi. Sorry. I just really missed you.
You answered! Okay. Okay. I’m not going to cry.
There you are. I thought you’d vanished.

default: Fine. I get the message. Bye.
Wow. Okay. Don’t bother calling back.
You could have just said. Bye.
thunderbirds: I don’t ring a man three times. Goodbye.
How very rude. Goodbye.
police: Noted. Don’t contact me again.
Understood. We’re done.
goth_girls: Ghosted by a man who still uses Hinge. Iconic. Bye.
Enjoy the silence. I will.
fourth_estate: No comment. Ever again. Bye.

warn: You don’t get to just ignore me.
Okay. Everyone’s going to know what you’re like.
Fine. Let’s see who picks up for you now.

tell.count: {her} messaged me. She says you’re talking to {count} of us at once. Is that true?
tell.ignore: {her} says you led her on and then stopped answering her calls. That’s cold.
tell.shown: {her} sent me screenshots of your messages to her. Interesting reading.
tell.married: {her} says you asked a girl to marry you after about a day. Do you say that to everyone?

spurn.toldBlock: Yeah, I don’t need this. Bye.

ad.title: PERSONAL
ad.summary: To the man on Hinge who never picks up.
ad.body: To the man on Hinge who never picks up his phone: I hope it was worth it. You know who you are. Now so does everyone else. {first}.

spurn.adMention: Is that personal ad in the paper about you? The one from {her}?
spurn.report: Your profile has been reported. Hinge has paused your matches while it takes a look.
voicemail: It’s me. I just wanted to hear your voice. Call me back.
Hi. It’s me again. Sorry. I miss you. That’s all.
I don’t know what I did. Please just call me.
I keep starting messages and deleting them. So. Voicemail. Call me.
It’s me. I’m not angry. I promise I’m not angry. Call me.
giveUp: Okay. I’ll stop. I’m here if you ever want me.
I’m going to stop calling now. I hope you’re okay.
This is the last one. Take care of yourself.

quiet: I’ve really liked talking to you. I’m going to take a break from the app for a while. Look after yourself.
I think I’ve said everything I know how to say over text. It was nice. Take care.
I’m deleting the app for a bit. Not because of you. Mostly because of everyone else.
This has been lovely, but I’m getting sucked into my phone again. I’m going quiet for a while.
My sister says I spend too long on here. She’s right. Bye for now.
I’m going to stop replying for a bit. If it’s meant to be, it’ll find a way.
Work’s about to eat me alive. I won’t be on here much. It was good talking.
I’m switching my phone off for a while. Thank you for the conversations.
callLead: Can I tell you something? I haven’t told anyone.
I wasn’t going to say this over text.
Okay. I rang because I wanted to tell someone.
You’re easy to talk to, so here it is.
I’ve been sitting on this all day.

pills.hook: Can’t sleep again? I’ve got something for that. I do a few shifts on the back counter at Desert Rx. You would not believe what gets thrown away.
pills.clue: {name} sells pills from the back counter at Desert Rx.

ask.label: Ask what she means by thrown away
ask.player: What do you mean, thrown away?
ask.reply: Sleeping pills, mostly. Some other things. Cash under your mat, and you never got them from me.

buy.label: Ask to buy some
buy.reply: Leave the cash under your mat tonight. Don’t take two.

warn.label: Tell her to stop before someone gets hurt
warn.player: You need to stop before someone gets hurt.
warn.reply: Says the man who can’t sleep. Fine. Maybe.

pills.delivered: A paper bag from Desert Rx, folded over twice, pushed through your letterbox. Inside: a brown bottle with no label.

item.label: A bag from Desert Rx
item.text: A brown bottle with no label, in a paper bag from Desert Rx. {first} sold it to you.

take.label: 💊 Take one tonight
take.notice: You sleep straight through to the next day. Your phone was on silent.

story.title: STUDENT IN HOSPITAL AFTER PILLS FROM A CAR PARK
story.summary: A 20-year-old student is recovering. Police want to know where the pills came from.
story.body: A university student, 20, is recovering in Sunfall General after taking pills bought in a supermarket car park. Detectives believe the pills came from a local pharmacy and are asking pharmacy staff to come forward.

tell.label: Tell her about the student in the paper
tell.player: Did you see the paper? A student nearly died.
tell.reply: I saw. I haven’t slept either. I’m done. I’m stopping. Today.

tip.label: Report a woman selling pills from Desert Rx
tip.reply: Desert Rx. Right. Leave it with us, love. And thank you.

arrested.title: PHARMACY WORKER ARRESTED OVER PILLS
arrested.summary: {name}, who worked the back counter at Desert Rx, has been charged.
arrested.body: {name} was arrested at Desert Rx and charged with supplying prescription drugs. Police say they are working through a list of her customers.

pills.friend: Did you report {first}? Everyone in our group is saying it was you.

husband.name: Wade
husband.clue: {name} is married. Her husband, Wade, has your number.
husband.open: Is this the man who keeps texting my wife? I’m {first}’s husband. Wade.
again: It’s Wade again. I’ve read more of them now.
You think I don’t know where she goes on her phone?
I’ve got your number. I can get the rest.
She says you’re just a friend. Are you just a friend?

choices.truth: Tell him the truth: you met on Hinge

husband.lie: Funny. You’re in her phone as Gym.
husband.friends: Friends don’t text her in the middle of the night.
husband.truth: Hinge. She told me she deleted it. A long silence. Right.
voicemail: This is Wade. You know who I am. Pick up.
Wade again. I’m not going to stop ringing.
I found your profile. Nice room.

ask.label: Ask her why she never mentioned a husband
ask.player: Your husband rang me. Why didn’t you tell me?
ask.reply: Because he’s never home, and when he is, he isn’t really there. I didn’t think you’d talk to me if you knew.

choices2.label: Tell her to leave him
choices2.player: Leave him. You deserve better than not really there.

choices2.label: Tell her you can’t do this
choices2.player: I can’t do this. I’m sorry.

choices2.label: Say it doesn’t matter to you
choices2.now: Good. Then nothing has to change.

leave.next: I did it. I’m at my sister’s. I feel sick and free at the same time.

truthNext.free: You told him. I should hate you. I’m at my sister’s. Honestly, I think you did me a favour.
truthNext.angry: You TOLD him? Do you know what you’ve done? Don’t ever message me again.

husband.leftCall: She’s gone. Her sister’s. I hope you’re pleased with yourself.
deaths: The car outside had been there all evening.
Someone had been waiting in the stairwell for a long time.

envelope.arrive: A padded envelope comes through your letterbox, addressed to T. Kessler, who had this room years ago. Inside: a thick fold of cash and a cheap phone.
envelope.clue: An envelope of cash for T. Kessler, who had your room years ago, was left on your doorstep. Someone wants it back.

item.label: An envelope for T. Kessler
item.text: A thick fold of cash and a cheap phone, addressed to T. Kessler, who had this room years ago.

take.label: 💵 Take some of the cash
take.notice: You take a few notes from the middle. Nobody will notice.

envelope.took: Someone has taken a few notes from the middle.
envelope.open: You’ve got something that isn’t yours. Don’t say a name. Put it back on the step tonight and we never talk again.
later: It’s still not on the step.
I know which door it is. I delivered it.
Tonight. On the step. Last time I ask nicely.

choices.step: Agree to leave it on the step
choices.police: Tell him you’ve called the police

envelope.stepReply: Good. Tonight. Then you forget this number.
envelope.policeReply: No, you haven’t. If you had, you wouldn’t still have it.
envelope.gone: The envelope has gone from the step. Someone has left a bottle of good whisky in a paper bag, just inside your door. No note.

gift.label: A bottle of whisky
gift.text: Good whisky in a paper bag, left at your door where the envelope had been. No note.

envelope.short: The envelope has gone from the step. Your phone rings once in the night. Nobody speaks.

tip.label: Report an envelope of cash left for an old tenant
tip.reply: Don’t touch it, and don’t answer that phone. An officer will collect it tonight.

envelope.collected: An officer collected the envelope overnight. Doreen says thank you.

news.title: CASH ON DOORSTEP LINKED TO MOTEL GANG
news.summary: A resident handed in an envelope left for a former tenant.
news.body: An envelope of cash, left on a doorstep for a former tenant, has been linked by detectives to a gang working out of the interstate motel.{short}

envelope.newsShort: Police say some of the money was missing.
deaths: They knew which door it was. They had delivered it.
The phone rang once, from somewhere inside the room.

cleaner.hook: I clean three houses up on the ridge. Bluebird houses. You would not believe what rich people leave lying around.
cleaner.clue: {name} steals from the Bluebird houses she cleans on the ridge.

ask.label: Ask what they leave lying around
ask.player: Like what?
ask.reply: Rings. Bracelets. Things nobody has worn in years. Nobody counts. Want a ring? For your future wife. Cheap.

buy.label: Buy a ring from her
buy.reply: Tomorrow, under your mat. Don’t wear it on the ridge.

warn.label: Tell her she’ll get caught
warn.reply: Nobody counts. That’s the whole point of being rich.

cleaner.delivered: A small velvet pouch, pushed under your door. Inside: an old diamond ring, far too good to be cheap.

item.label: A diamond ring (don’t ask)
item.text: An old diamond ring in a velvet pouch, from {first}. Far too good to be cheap.

story.title: HEIRLOOM RING MISSING FROM RIDGE HOME
story.summary: The Ashworth family say a diamond ring has vanished.
story.body: A diamond ring that has been in the Ashworth family for four generations has gone missing from their home on the ridge. Mrs Constance Ashworth said nobody had worn it in years, but she noticed at once. Police are speaking to domestic staff.

tip.label: Report a cleaner stealing from the ridge houses
tip.reply: The ridge. Right. We’ll have a word with the agency. Thank you, love.

handIn.label: Hand in a ring you were sold
handIn.reply: Hand it in? Good lad. Leave it in an envelope by the door and an officer will collect it. Nobody needs to know where it came from.

cleaner.handedNotice: An officer collected the ring. Doreen says the Ashworths will be very glad.

tb.label: Tell her about the Ashworths’ cleaner
tb.player: I think I know who took the Ashworths’ ring. Their cleaner.
tb.reply: The Ashworths’ cleaner? Leave it with me. Constance will be very grateful.

cleaner.thanks: The Ashworths are telling everyone you handed in that ring. Well done, you.

arrested.title: CLEANER CHARGED OVER RIDGE THEFTS
arrested.summary: {name} cleaned three homes on the ridge.
arrested.body: {name}, who cleaned three homes on the ridge, has been charged with theft. Police say they are tracing everything she sold.

cleaner.friend: Did you have something to do with {first} getting arrested?

watch.name: Constance Ashworth
watch.clue: Constance Ashworth chairs the Ridge Neighbourhood Watch. She keeps a file on everyone in Sunfall.
watch.open: Constance Ashworth. I chair the Ridge Neighbourhood Watch. You’re the young man who is always at home. We have a use for people who are always at home.
watch.openRing: Constance Ashworth. You’re the young man who found my ring. I chair the Ridge Neighbourhood Watch, and I have a use for people who are always at home.
watch.what: Information. Who comes and goes. Who says what. Girls talk to you, I gather. I keep a file on everyone in Sunfall. I would like to keep one with you, rather than on you.
watch.joined: Splendid. I’ll ring. Have something for me.
watch.refused: How disappointing. You have a window, you know. Everyone does.
watch.ask: Constance Ashworth. Well? Tell me something about one of your girls.
watch.took: How interesting. Thank you. The Bluebirds will hear good things about you.
watch.nothing: Nothing? I do hope that isn’t becoming a habit.
watch.page: A cream envelope through your letterbox, with the Ashworth crest. Inside: one typed page from the Watch file. It’s about you.

pageItem.label: A page from the Watch file
pageItem.text: One typed page under the Ashworth crest: your name, your window, the time your light goes off, and the names of the women you talk to.

watch.betrayed: How does Constance Ashworth know what I told you? I told YOU that. Nobody else. Don’t ever message me again.

column.title: WHAT THE WATCH KNOWS
column.summary: A local woman’s private business, courtesy of an anonymous friend.
column.body: The Ridge Neighbourhood Watch notes that {name} has not been entirely honest with the people around her. An anonymous friend tells us more.

watch.window: Constance Ashworth showed me a photograph of you at your window at night. Every night. Explain.

newsroom.label: Tell the newsroom about Constance Ashworth’s files
newsroom.noProof: A neighbourhood watch with files on everyone? Get us one page and we’ll run it.
newsroom.proof: One page is all we need. This runs tomorrow.

expose.title: WATCH CHAIR KEPT SECRET FILES ON RESIDENTS
expose.summary: Typed pages seen by the Sunfall Daily list who comes and goes, and when lights go off.
expose.body: Constance Ashworth, chair of the Ridge Neighbourhood Watch, kept typed files on hundreds of Sunfall residents, the Sunfall Daily can reveal. Mrs Ashworth said she was simply being neighbourly.

watch.exposedCall: You. Do you know how long I have kept this town in order? Enjoy your window.
watch.tbCool: Did you go to the paper about Constance? Half the club isn’t speaking to the other half.
watch.othersWarm: Was it you who exposed that Ashworth woman? She had a file on my mum. Thank you.
